Phase 3 derisked with Department of War (DoW) funding.
In February 2026, iX received a sole-source US$40.95mn DoW award to fund Wafermine's EUA work and Phase 3 programme.

Sole-source awards are made when the US Government determines that only one supplier can meet its requirement.

These span men's and women's health, weight management and longevity.
The company estimates the US compounding market at US$10.7bn by 2033.
Management expects B2B sales to begin in 1Q CY2027, and we forecast c.S$20mn of compounding revenue in FY28F.

The Company has tested absorption and pharmacokinetics (PK) in humans across numerous active drug compounds, including buprenorphine, ketamine and dexmedetomidine.
Wafermine® has completed seven clinical studies involving 320 participants, including a Phase 2b study on safety and efficacy.

One of these, a published Phase 1 study in eight healthy male participants reported absolute bioavailability of approximately 29% for a 25mg sublingual ketamine wafer.
Ketamine was first quantifiable in plasma within five minutes, while median time to maximum concentration was approximately 0.75 hours. The formulation was reported to have good local tolerability.
This study shows that the wafer can deliver ketamine rapidly. While clinical data are most advanced for Wafermine® and other formulations remain at earlier stages, this human evidence reduces platform risk relative to a technology supported only by laboratory testing.

title: Keppel DC REIT: Where the Growth Is Coming From, and the Risks to Watch
article:
Keppel DC REIT
(SGX: AJBU) grew its
distribution per unit
(DPU) in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026).
DPU rose 11.3% year on year to S$0.05714, while distributable income grew even faster, up 18.5% to S$150.7 million.

Positive rental reversions and escalations lifted income.
The REIT also bought Tokyo Data Centre 3 and, in February 2026, completed its purchase of the remaining interests in Keppel DC Singapore 3 and 4.
But that’s only part of the story.
Where is the growth coming from?
Demand for data centres is still the main engine.
The REIT manager points to forecasts that global data centre capacity will grow 25% a year to reach 256 GW by 2030.
What’s holding back the new supply isn’t money.
It’s power.
According to Keppel DC REIT, the hardest part of building a data centre is securing enough electricity and a grid connection, then winning planning approval.
These hurdles are steepest in established “Tier 1” markets such as Singapore, Japan and the major European hubs, where land and power are in short supply.
That scarcity plays to Keppel DC REIT’s strengths.
The REIT already owns operating data centres in exactly these markets, and clients have contracted around 95% of the power capacity it can earn revenue from.
How is Keppel DC REIT paying for its growth?
With more debt, though on better terms than a year ago:
Average cost of debt fell to 2.6% in 1H 2026 from 3.0% a year ago.
Interest cover rose to 6.9 times from 5.9 times.
Fixed-rate debt rose to 87% of borrowings from 76%.
A bigger debt load still costs more.
Total borrowings grew from S$1.6 billion in 1H 2025 to around S$2.3 billion in 1H 2026, and finance costs climbed 25.2% year on year to S$30.7 million.
Gearing rose to 34% from 30%.
In short, Keppel DC REIT is carrying more debt at a lower
interest rate
.
That trade-off works as long as the newly acquired assets earn more than they cost, and net property income (NPI) growth of 15.1% to S$210.4 million suggests they do.
What are the risks?
Internet enterprise clients, mostly hyperscalers, accounted for 70.4% of rental income as of 30 June 2026, up from 67.4% a year earlier.
Here’s the rub: Keppel DC REIT’s single largest client contributes 43.5%.
This concentration cuts both ways.
Hyperscalers generally have higher credit quality and give investors direct exposure to AI-driven demand.
Unfortunately, Keppel DC REIT has not named its largest client.
Meanwhile, portfolio occupancy slipped to 92.5% in 1H 2026 from 95.8% a year ago.
Almost all of the decline comes from Cardiff Data Centre, whose contract expired in June 2026 and which now sits vacant.
Strip Cardiff out and portfolio occupancy would be 95.3%.
A few other assets still need work.
Keppel DC Singapore 1 remains at 46.5% occupancy after the non-renewal of its non-data-centre space, which makes up a significant portion of the asset.
The sale of Basis Bay, which has 40.2% occupancy, is taking longer than expected.
Keppel DC REIT announced the divestment on 2 January 2025 and had targeted completion by 3Q 2025.
In Guangdong, the manager has committed to no significant capital expenditure on its troubled data centres as it explores exit options.
Related articles:
Top 4 S-REITs Raising DPU by 10% or More
The “Data Centre” Gold Mine: Keppel DC REIT vs. Digital Core REIT
Get Smart: Follow the rent back to who pays it
Keppel DC REIT owns data centres in markets where power limits new supply, and that position supports its growth.
A distribution, though, is only as dependable as the tenants who pay the rent.
When one client contributes 43.5%, that client’s financial health matters as much as the industry’s growth.
So before you weigh up any REIT’s DPU growth, ask yourself: how much of the rent comes from the biggest tenant, and how confident are you that it will keep paying?
The answer may give you a clue as to whether you should buy the REIT.

title: Asian stocks to fall as hot US inflation data sparks Wall Street selloff
article:
(Oct 15): Asian stocks were set to decline, tracking a tech-led Wall Street selloff after hotter-than-expected US inflation fueled bets on more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes. The dollar rose.

Equity-index futures for Japan, South Korea and Australia all declined, putting a regional stock gauge on course for a fourth straight day of losses. Wall Street contracts pointed lower after the S&P 500 Index dropped 1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 suffered its steepest slide since late July. The Russell 2000 entered a correction.

Technology shares bore the brunt of the selloff as higher rate expectations added to concerns over lofty valuations and the enormous cost of building artificial-intelligence infrastructure. A closely watched gauge of semiconductor stocks including Nvidia Corp. and Broadcom Inc. dropped for a sixth day, its longest losing streak since May 2025.

Earlier, the fastest US inflation in five months prompted traders to ramp up bets on further Fed tightening, raising the prospect of additional rate hikes even if policymakers pause in October. While Treasuries initially sank after the data was announced, they recovered most of the losses on appetite for bond yields near multiyear highs. Gold slumped.

Stubborn US inflation, fueled by elevated oil prices since the Middle East war broke out, is raising the prospect of more aggressive Fed rate hikes. At the same time, equity markets are coming under pressure after a blistering rally in AI-related stocks, bringing the US market’s longest stretch of tranquility since before the Covid-19 pandemic to an end.

“With broadening inflation pressures becoming more evident in today’s CPI report, the Fed is increasingly at risk of falling behind the curve in containing inflation,” wrote Ronald Temple, chief market strategist for Lazard’s Financial Advisory and Asset Management businesses.

See also: Asian stocks rise on signal Fed may not need aggressive rate hikes

The consumer price index rose 0.6% in September from a month earlier, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data out Wednesday, and climbed 3.7% from a year earlier. The move was driven by rising fuel costs, while a gauge of underlying price pressures also rose more than expected.

See also: ICE plans futures for livestock in a bid to challenge CME Group

The two-year Treasury yield jumped as much as 16 basis points after the inflation reading before ending two basis points higher, while the five-year topped 5.15% for the first time since 2007. The 10-year yield fell two basis points to 5.19%.

The dollar rose to its highest in more than a year, extending its longest weekly winning streak since early 2025 as traders ramped up Fed tightening bets. Markets now price about 40 basis points of hikes by the end of January, with the odds of an October move also rising.

“It’s clear as ever that inflation is stubborn and moving in the wrong direction,” said Skyler Weinand at Regan Capital. “While we expect the Fed to pause on any rate changes in October, we expect rate hikes to resume in December.”

Precious metals tumbled as the inflation surprise pushed rate expectations higher. Gold slumped, silver fell to its lowest since July 20, and platinum and palladium also declined.

Elsewhere, US oil inched higher in early Asian trading as escalating hostilities from Russia to the Middle East threatened supply flows that had only recently recovered toward pre-war levels.

Brent settled above US$106 a barrel after Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched missile and drone strikes across Saudi Arabia, including an attack that damaged Saudi Aramco’s headquarters. The strikes added to an escalation in Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening the recovery in Gulf supply.

“Developments over the past week are yet another reminder that recovering flows are not the same as secure flows,” said Emily Ashford, head of energy research at Standard Chartered Bank. “With both infrastructure and shipping increasingly vulnerable, the risk premium is proving difficult to unwind.”

title: Oil holds gain as Middle East and Russia strikes threaten supply
article:
(Oct 15): Oil held a gain as a flare-up in attacks from Russia to the Middle East threatened supply that only recently recovered to near pre-war levels.

West Texas Intermediate held near US$95 a barrel, after rising 1% on Wednesday. Brent settled around US$106. A cargo ship sank after being struck by “unknown projectiles” as it transited the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran-backed Houthis continued to launch missile and drone attacks across Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, Russia accused Ukraine of attacking two oil refineries on Wednesday, flouting an “energy ceasefire” promoted by US President Donald Trump. Kyiv denied the claim, which Bloomberg couldn’t independently verify.

Brent has surged more than 70% this year as the US-Iran war roils energy markets. The depletion of stocks during the fighting has left global observed inventories 509 million barrels below pre-conflict levels, and on-land stockpiles near their lowest in at least a decade, the International Energy Agency said Wednesday, warning that supplies of diesel and other fuels will remain under pressure next year.

“If new attacks on oil infrastructure in the Middle East further disrupt petroleum supply in an already very tight physical market, energy costs and inflation would move even higher,” said Bart Melek, global head of commodity strategy at TD Securities.

Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Ukrainian drones targeted refineries in the Saratov and Ryazan regions, Interfax reported. Ryazan, near Moscow, has a processing capacity of about 400,000 barrels a day and is among the largest oil refineries in the nation.

See also: Oil rises as Middle East attacks increase uncertainty over flows

In the Middle East, a growing number of oil tankers are avoiding areas where they would normally collect crude, suggesting increased Iranian attacks on shipping are complicating export logistics. Vessels capable of carrying at least 37 million barrels have stopped or changed course while heading toward loading areas off the United Arab Emirates and Oman, though there’s no clear evidence yet that Gulf flows have declined.

Prospects for a diplomatic easing of tensions remain uncertain. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Islamic Republic’s aims aren’t “Endless War’ or prolonged talks, but that it seeks to “wear down the enemy so that it is forced to accept our demands.”

Meanwhile, oil production in the UAE climbed to record levels last month, according to the IEA. The former OPEC member has been one of the most successful regional producers in restoring flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

See also: Trump’s diesel deal irks allies and is unlikely to reduce prices

In the US, the industry-funded American Petroleum Institute reported nationwide crude inventories fell 11.1 million barrels last week, according to a document seen by Bloomberg. If confirmed by official data on Thursday, that would be the biggest drop since June 2025.
• WTI for November delivery slipped 0.3% to US$94.77 a barrel at 7:13 a.m. in Singapore.
• Brent for December gained 0.4% to settle at US$106.06 a barrel on Wednesday.

title: US stocks fall on inflation woes as chip rout deepens
article:
(Oct 15): Stocks fell the most since July as a selloff in chipmakers extended a decline that was fueled by wagers the Federal Reserve will keep lifting interest rates to fight inflation.

The broad upswing in consumer prices reinforced bets on rate hikes even if the Fed pauses in October. The S&P 500 snapped its longest streak without a 1% drop in over six years. The Russell 2000 entered a correction. A gauge of chip giants sank 4.3%. CoreWeave Inc.’s bonds hit levels that usually signal distress. Its chief said the market is acting “irrationally.”

A closely watched measure of semiconductor powerhouses such as Nvidia Corp. and Broadcom Inc. extended a six-day drop to about 12% amid mounting concerns about higher rates, lofty valuations and the massive cost of building artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

“While increased competition within AI, rising financing requirements, and higher rates may periodically add to volatility, we view this latest bout as more of a recalibration of expectations than a fundamental break in the AI investment story,” said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office.

The equity retreat kindled investor demand for bonds with yields near multi-year highs. The latest inflation data had earlier triggered a plunge in Treasuries, prompting traders to briefly price in two Fed hikes by the end of January. Those bets faded. The dollar hit the highest since May 2025.

“It’s clear as ever that inflation is stubborn and moving in the wrong direction,” said Skyler Weinand at Regan Capital. “While we expect the Fed to pause on any rate changes in October, we expect rate hikes to resume in December.”

See also: Stocks bounce from lows on Williams’ rate remarks

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has vowed not to steer markets with his own near-term outlook for monetary policy. But the inflation surprise will heighten scrutiny of his remarks late Thursday New York time in Bangkok, where he is scheduled to appear in a fireside chat with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva.

Inflation pressures are broadening beyond energy, suggesting the last mile back to target could remain bumpy and keep rates elevated, according to Jeff Roach at LPL Financial. The latest report complicates the Fed’s decision this month as the road back to price stability is looking increasingly difficult to navigate, he added.

The question is whether firmer core inflation is enough to alter the Fed’s path, according to Seema Shah at Principal Asset Management. Markets are clearly unsettled, but the latest report is not strong enough to revive the case for an October hike, she said.

See also: S&P 500 holds firm as banks report earnings, chipmakers slump

While the latest consumer price index raises concerns around inflation risks, the Fed has already communicated a gradual hiking process, according to TD Securities’ strategists including Oscar Munoz and Gennadiy Goldberg.

“Today’s report makes the chance of an October hike higher, but we still believe the Fed will hold and opt for December as the market is already doing some of the work for them,” they said.
• Apple Inc. is gearing up to release its artificial-intelligence platform in mainland China, following a lengthy regulatory delay that has kept the company’s AI features out of one of its most important markets.
• Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted.
• Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., Dell Technologies Inc. and NetApp Inc. were downgraded to equal-weight at Barclays, which cited the recent “significant” stock run and a more cautious approach on the stocks given the enterprise spending environment.
• Bank of America Corp.’s stock and fixed-income traders missed estimates as the bank’s results were also hurt by a charge tied to regulatory penalties over money laundering and sanctions violations.
• Morgan Stanley’s third-quarter profit climbed as the firm’s equity traders trounced analysts’ estimates and the wealth-management operation brought in a record amount of money.
• BlackRock Inc. pulled in US$205 billion of new money in the third quarter as revenue surged at the world’s largest asset manager, which is now a full year into a major transformation to push further into higher-fee private markets.
